answer: Each candidate identity must complete a prescribed sequence of modular squarings, where every step depends on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the result efficiently. GPUs cannot parallelize a single identity’s chain, so creating many clones requires running many chains and paying their compute and elapsed-time costs. This bottleneck raises the cost of Sybil attacks, though mirror checks, meadow records, or a vault of proofs cannot replace the delay.
